reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology employs a pipeline integrating computer vision and machine learning to automate trampoline skill identification. Starting with a single video feed, each frame undergoes pose estimation using a convolutional neural network (CNN), extracting key joint locations. These are then processed into body orientation and joint angle trajectories over time. Each trajectory is compared against a database of known skill motions using a nearest neighbor classifier with mean squared error (MSE) as the similarity metric. This approach leverages the temporal dynamics of body movement to distinguish between different skills, such as tucks, pikes, or straddles. The system assumes consistent viewing angles and sufficient visibility of body parts, but may fail under occlusion or inconsistent lighting. The robustness of this framework stems from its reliance on empirical motion patterns rather than symbolic rule sets, allowing it to generalize across variations in performer technique while maintaining high classification accuracy (80.7%) on a dataset of 714 skill examples.
